evidence: This is a proposal based on the findings of the study.

claim: Talpid3 cells have abnormal microtubule dynamics.
source: Talpid3 cells have abnormal microtubule dynamics (Yin et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Microtubules are required for the recruitment of satellites and proteins in the distal centriole.
source: Microtubules are required for the recruitment of satellites and proteins in the distal centriole (Kim et al., 2008; Schmidt et al., 2009), a process known to be impaired by loss of KIAA0586.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Abnormal cell polarity in talpid3 cells may be due to the effect of TALPID3 on microtubule dynamics and a direct role in centrosome organization.
source: Abnormal cell polarity in talpid3 cells may be due to the effect of TALPID3 on microtubule dynamics and a direct role in centrosome organization: microtubules are essential for intracellular trafficking, cellular structure, and polarity.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the cell polarity defects.

claim: Microtubules are essential for intracellular trafficking, cellular structure, and polarity.
source: Abnormal cell polarity in talpid3 cells may be due to the effect of TALPID3 on microtubule dynamics and a direct role in centrosome organization: microtubules are essential for intracellular trafficking, cellular structure, and polarity.

claim: Localization of the centrosome, mitochondria, and Golgi is disrupted in talpid3 cells.

source: Moreover, Rab8, a GTPase which binds to the Golgi and is required for vesicular trafficking and ciliogenesis (Nachury et al., 2007; Henry and Sheff, 2008; Feng et al., 2012), is mislocalized in KIAA0586-depleted cells (Kobayashi et al., 2014a).

claim: In JBTS patients with mutations in AHI1 (JBTS3), encoding an interactor of RAB8, non-ciliary trafficking from the Golgi and ciliogenesis are impaired.
source: In JBTS patients with mutations in AHI1 (JBTS3), encoding an interactor of RAB8 (Hsiao et al., 2009), non-ciliary trafficking from the Golgi and ciliogenesis are impaired.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Golgi mislocalization in the talpid3 choroid plexus is similar to what has been observed in Ahi1−/− mice.
source: Of note, Golgi mislocalization in the talpid3 choroid plexus is similar to what has been observed in Ahi1−/− mice (Hsiao et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

source: This suggests a similar pathogenesis of JBTS23 and JBTS3, with defective cell polarity, intracellular trafficking, and Hh signaling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarities between the phenotypes.

claim: KIAA0586 interacts with CP110 and Cep120, distal centriolar proteins implicated in centriole duplication and maturation, and ciliogenesis.
source: KIAA0586 interacts with CP110 and Cep120 (Kobayashi et al., 2014a), distal centriolar proteins implicated in centriole duplication and maturation, and ciliogenesis.

source: The predominant expression of Cep120 on the daughter centriole throughout most of the cell cycle depends on Kiaa0586, as indicated by high expression of Cep120 on both centrioles and absence of CP110 from the mother centriole prior to ciliogenesis in Talpid3−/− cells (Spektor et al., 2007).

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

source: In addition, loss of chicken KIAA0586 (TALPID3) causes centriole elongation whereas overexpression of Cep120 causes elongation of the mother centriole, suggesting that KIAA0586 (TALPID3) may control centriole length through depletion or suppression of Cep120 on the mother centriole.

claim: Overexpression of Cep120 causes elongation of the mother centriole.
source: In addition, loss of chicken KIAA0586 (TALPID3) causes centriole elongation whereas overexpression of Cep120 causes elongation of the mother centriole, suggesting that KIAA0586 (TALPID3) may control centriole length through depletion or suppression of Cep120 on the mother centriole.

claim: KIAA0586 (TALPID3) may control centriole length through depletion or suppression of Cep120 on the mother centriole.
source: In addition, loss of chicken KIAA0586 (TALPID3) causes centriole elongation whereas overexpression of Cep120 causes elongation of the mother centriole, suggesting that KIAA0586 (TALPID3) may control centriole length through depletion or suppression of Cep120 on the mother centriole.

claim: It has been proposed that KIAA0586 regulates ciliary vesicle docking adjacent to Cep164 localization, but not distal appendage formation itself.
source: Based on the colocalization of KIAA0586, CP110, and Cep164, it has been proposed that KIAA0586 regulates ciliary vesicle docking adjacent to Cep164 localization (Kobayashi et al., 2014a), but not distal appendage formation itself, and this is supported by evidence from human patient KIAA0586−/− cells which show Cep164 within the distal centriole (Alby et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Evidence from human patient KIAA0586−/− cells shows Cep164 within the distal centriole, supporting the proposal that KIAA0586 does not regulate distal appendage formation itself.
source: Based on the colocalization of KIAA0586, CP110, and Cep164, it has been proposed that KIAA0586 regulates ciliary vesicle docking adjacent to Cep164 localization (Kobayashi et al., 2014a), but not distal appendage formation itself, and this is supported by evidence from human patient KIAA0586−/− cells which show Cep164 within the distal centriole (Alby et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: KIAA0586 loss primarily causes abnormal distal appendages and impaired Cep164 localization, similar to what can be observed in OFD1 mutants.
source: We also find evidence for a vesicle docking defect, demonstrated by an increase in centriolar satellites. claim: Determination of Cep164 expression in cells of highly polarized tissue demonstrates a loss of centriole orientation to the apical membrane of the cell.
source: In addition, determination of Cep164 expression in cells of highly polarized tissue demonstrates a further centriolar defect not easily distinguished in in vitro assays—the loss of centriole orientation to the apical membrane of the cell.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on Cep164 immunofluorescence in polarized tissue.

claim: Whether the defect in centriole orientation is due to the depletion of KIAA0586 from the centriole or impairment of another function of KIAA0586 in pericentriolar regions or cytoskeleton remains to be elucidated.
source: Whether this defect is due to the depletion of KIAA0586 from the centriole or impairment of another function of KIAA0586 in pericentriolar regions or cytoskeleton remains to be elucidated.

source: We have identified KIAA0586 as a novel gene for JBTS, and we propose that it is not only required for ciliogenesis, but also to establish cell and thus tissue polarity.
